protocol.boot_interruption: Six accepted old-build pairs preceded a host reboot. The resumed measurement completed the remaining pairs; structural trials use the new reservation and boot identity.
protocol.final_capacity_attempt: The first final controller collected zero trials because its short Rust-capacity wait expired. It restored CI scheduling. The retry allows a bounded 30-minute capacity wait; lease waits remain outside timing.
protocol.memory_boundary: VmHWM before full-fact fingerprinting. Resident scenarios include untimed initial restoration; their high-water readings do not isolate mutation allocation.
protocol.pmu: Unprivileged perf task-clock was denied with perf_event_paranoid=4. A privileged known-nonzero probe succeeded (1280009 cycles, 854966 instructions, 34246 cache misses). Phase-attributed PMU counters were not collected for the benchmark; timing alone does not identify an allocator/cache cause.
protocol.readiness_boundary: Restore or mutation return, before the separately timed registered Cypher, word, trigram, and literal queries. All queries must pass before a trial counts. The host counter marker also includes their execution.
protocol.v3_io_accounting: Historical posting-stage trials recorded global and own full-pressure durations and bounded their nonnegative difference. Full pressure means all non-idle tasks in a group stall together, so the difference is a weak attribution instrument across differently sized groups. Preserve the readings and acceptance flags; they do not prove an external-I/O bound. The final artifact is repeated under v4. Posting-stage unchanged restarts retain their v2 whole-system full-pressure gate.
protocol.v4_final_artifact: Repeat all eight workloads with three accepted pairs each on the final artifact. Preflight uses system-wide SOME I/O pressure; during the benchmark, bound the nonnegative difference between system and own-cgroup SOME pressure at readiness and completion. SOME records intervals with any stalled task. This difference is a heuristic estimate: overlapping external I/O and counter aggregation/windowing limit attribution. A dedicated external writer must produce nonzero pressure and fire the 2% rejection gate. Before/after graph parity is required except batch64: its baseline loses imported-module CALLS after recovery; the fixed artifact must match the known full fresh-build graph digest, edge count, and resolved-call count. Posting/corpus/file/node parity remains required in every workload. Known snapshot writes with material global SOME pressure must read nonzero own-cgroup SOME pressure.
protocol.write_gate_correction: v2 incorrectly treated the benchmark snapshot writer as external I/O. Those write trials were retained as rejected and rerun prospectively under v3; no old acceptance flags were changed.
